papers.title: EEG-Driven Decoding Framework for Passenger Hazard Perception in Highly Automated Vehicles
papers.reason: The paper decodes human EEG responses during hazard perception, providing attention- and decision-related neural findings relevant to executive-function assessment, although its primary focus is vehicle safety rather than cognitive process modelling.

papers.title: Non-convulsive status epilepticus revealing acute deterioration in AARS2 mutation–associated progressive leukoencephalopathy
papers.reason: The title describes an acute neurological case without evidence of executive-function modelling, relevant cognitive findings, or cognitive assessment methodology.

papers.title: Concurrent Multidomain Cognitive Assessment and Serum BDNF Level in Aged Dogs: Comparison Between Normal Cognition and Mild Cognitive Impairment
papers.reason: The study identifies delayed match-to-sample and object-recognition measures that distinguish cognitively normal from mildly impaired aged dogs, directly informing behavioural screening for early impairment.

papers.title: Motor Imagery Acquisition and Classification Using a Low-Cost 8-Channel EEG System in a VR ADHD Serious Game Environment: A Case Study
papers.reason: The paper demonstrates low-cost EEG classification in an ADHD-oriented cognitive-training environment, but focuses on technical motor-imagery feasibility rather than executive-function assessment or clinical-group discrimination.

papers.title: Reconceptualising complex needs in later life: a multidimensional framework for integrated person-centred care
papers.reason: Cognitive decline is only contextual background for a proposed integrated-care framework that does not model, measure, or classify executive function.

papers.title: Neurocognitive Changes and Cerebral Blood Flow in Patients with Symptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis before and after Carotid Endarterectomy.
papers.reason: The longitudinal association between cerebral blood-flow recovery and MoCA improvement provides relevant neurovascular evidence, although executive-function domains are not analysed specifically.

papers.title: Impact of Metabolic Dysregulation on Cognitive Performance in Women with Gestational Diabetes Mellitus
papers.reason: The study relates metabolic dysregulation to MoCA performance, but its only domain-specific result concerns delayed recall rather than executive function or working memory.

papers.title: ADAS-Cog performance in urban Indian Alzheimer's patients: Implications for culturally appropriate assessment
papers.reason: The paper addresses culturally appropriate Alzheimer's assessment, but its small cross-sectional analysis emphasizes memory and language rather than executive-function or multimodal digital biomarkers.
